security_audit.summary: I reviewed the single Markdown skill and found the static alerts are false positives caused by code fences, inline code terms, a placeholder universal-link URL, and route parameter names. The skill contains Expo Router navigation guidance and does not include executable scripts, prompt injection text, data exfiltration instructions, or malicious network behavior.

static_findings.snippet: Expo Router uses file-system based routing. Files in `app/` become routes.
See `rn-auth` skill for full auth context pattern. Key navigation piece:
| Screen not found | Check file name matches route, check `_layout.tsx` includes screen |
| Tabs not showing | Ensure tab screens are direct children of tab `_layout.tsx` |
| Back button missing | Check `headerShown` in parent and child layouts |
| Deep link not working | Verify scheme in app.json, test with `uri-scheme` CLI |

content.user_title: Build Expo Router Navigation for React Native
content.value_statement: React Native teams need predictable navigation across tabs, stacks, modals, and deep links. This skill provides Expo Router patterns for common routing decisions.
actual_capabilities: Explains Expo Router file-based routes, layout groups, dynamic routes, and catch-all routes.
Shows programmatic navigation patterns using push, replace, back, navigate, and dismiss actions.
Provides Link component examples for simple links, route parameters, child buttons, and replacement navigation.
Covers stack, tab, modal, and dynamic header configuration for Expo Router layouts.
Gives deep-link and universal-link setup examples for Expo apps.
Lists practical debugging checks for common navigation problems.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not modify project files automatically.
It focuses on Expo Router, not standalone React Navigation without Expo Router.
It references authentication navigation only at the routing level, not full auth implementation.
Examples are simplified and must be adapted to each app state model and type system.

use_cases.title: Plan a New App Navigation Structure
use_cases.description: Create a clear Expo Router route tree with tabs, stacks, dynamic pages, and fallback screens.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Routing Patterns
use_cases.description: Document consistent choices for modals, protected routes, deep links, and navigation parameters.

use_cases.title: Debug Navigation Behavior
use_cases.description: Check common causes when tabs, headers, params, back behavior, or deep links do not work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Route Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Expo Router app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the rn-navigation skill to design a simple Expo Router route structure for an app with Home, Profile, Settings, and a Not Found screen.

prompt_templates.title: Add Dynamic Navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the rn-navigation skill to show how I should navigate from a list screen to a detail screen with a typed route parameter.

prompt_templates.title: Design Auth and Modal Flows
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the rn-navigation skill to plan an Expo Router layout with auth screens, main tabs, a booking modal, and safe redirects after login.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex Navigation Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing app design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the rn-navigation skill to review my Expo Router structure and identify likely causes of broken tabs, missing headers, wrong params, or failed deep links.

output_examples.input: I need bottom tabs for Home and Profile, plus a player detail screen outside the tabs.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a tab group for Home and Profile, a root stack for the player detail screen, and a route parameter for the player identifier.

output_examples.input: My deep link opens the app but does not reach the expected screen.
output_examples.output: The skill would guide checks for the app scheme, universal-link domain settings, route file names, and parsed incoming URL path.

output_examples.input: After login, users can go back to the login screen.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend replacement navigation after login and a protected route check that redirects authenticated users away from auth screens.

best_practices: Keep route names aligned with the app directory so file paths and URLs stay predictable.
Use replacement navigation after login, onboarding, or completed flows that should not remain in history.
Use URL parameters for simple shareable state and global state for larger transient objects.
anti_patterns: Do not pass complex objects through URL parameters when shared state or cached data is safer.
Do not hide navigation problems by disabling headers or gestures without checking parent layouts.
Do not assume deep links work until the scheme, universal-link domain, and route path are tested.

faq.question: What navigation library does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Expo Router patterns for React Native apps.

faq.question: Can it help with tab navigation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes tab layout examples and guidance for tab screen placement.

faq.question: Does it include deep-link guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers custom schemes, universal links, and incoming link handling.

faq.question: Does it implement authentication?
faq.answer: No. It only shows navigation checks and redirects for authenticated and unauthenticated routes.

faq.question: Can it debug missing parameters?
faq.answer: Yes. It points users toward route file names, parameter hooks, and link construction issues.

faq.question: Is this skill useful for non-Expo apps?
faq.answer: Only partially. Its examples assume Expo Router and Expo project conventions.
